title: Biomod Affiliate Program Agreement
body:
BIOMOD AFFILIATE PROGRAM AGREEMENT

1. Parties and acceptance

This Affiliate Program Agreement governs participation in the invitation-only TryBioMod affiliate program operated by BM Trade LLC (Company). Access is limited to recipients authorized by the Company. An invitation or forwarded link does not itself confer approval or commission eligibility. The person or entity applying to participate is the Affiliate. The program terms identify the Company, agreement version, $500 minimum payout and 30-day payment cycle. A separate individual Program Schedule identifies the Affiliate, associated agreement version, commission percentage, hold period and payment method selected by the Company for that Affiliate. There is no automatic or uniform commission percentage, hold period or payment method. The Affiliate must affirmatively accept the individual Program Schedule before any new order qualifies for commission. It forms part of this Agreement and must be available for review before acceptance.

By affirmatively accepting this Agreement through the Affiliate's authenticated account, the Affiliate agrees to the displayed version and Program Schedule. A person accepting for an entity represents that they have authority to bind it. Acceptance records do not constitute Company approval. Participation begins only after the Company approves the application and assigns an active referral code. The Affiliate must be at least 21 years old, supply accurate information and maintain current contact information.

2. Relationship and permitted activity

The Affiliate is an independent contractor, not an employee, agent, distributor, franchisee or legal partner of the Company. Neither party may bind the other. Participation is nonexclusive. The Affiliate is responsible for its own expenses and applicable taxes. No purchase, inventory investment or enrollment fee is required to participate. Compensation is based on qualifying product sales, not recruiting other affiliates. No sales volume, income or continued participation is guaranteed.

The Company grants an approved Affiliate a limited, nonexclusive, nontransferable, revocable permission to use Company-provided names, marks, links and promotional materials solely to promote eligible products through approved channels under this Agreement. The Company retains ownership of its marks and materials; the Affiliate retains ownership of its preexisting work. The Affiliate may not impersonate the Company, register confusingly similar domains or accounts, change scientific product information or certificates, or sublicense Company materials. Separate written permission is required for paid advertising using Company marks or bidding on those marks as keywords.

3. Advertising standards and disclosures

All promotional statements must be truthful, accurate, supportable and consistent with the product's actual identity and the Company's approved information. Affiliates must not make express or implied claims of disease treatment, prevention or cure; promise weight loss or other health outcomes; suggest approval by a regulator that has not approved the product; or represent a certificate of analysis as evidence of clinical efficacy or safety for human use.

Products designated for laboratory research must be described as laboratory research products. Affiliates must not promote human or animal consumption, dosing, injection, reconstitution, mixing instructions, clinical protocols or before-and-after outcomes. A research-use disclaimer does not excuse contradictory statements, imagery or implications. Affiliates must not target minors or encourage unlawful uses or purchases.

The Affiliate must clearly disclose its financial relationship with the Company wherever it recommends products or presents referral links or codes. A suitable statement is: “I earn a commission from Biomod on orders through my link or code.” Disclosures must be easy to notice, understand and associate with the endorsement, in the same language as the promotion. They must not be confined to a profile, separate terms page, collapsed text or an unrelated link. Video promotions must include appropriate visible and spoken disclosures; live broadcasts must repeat disclosures sufficiently for viewers joining later. A platform disclosure tool may supplement, but does not replace, an effective disclosure in the content itself.

The Affiliate must not fabricate experiences, testimonials or reviews; purchase positive reviews; condition incentives on favorable opinions; use undisclosed paid endorsements; or imply that Company approval substitutes for compliance with applicable law or platform requirements. The Company may request copies of promotional materials and require correction or removal of noncompliant content. The Affiliate must stop new distribution promptly upon notice and remove or correct content under its control as soon as reasonably practicable, ordinarily within two business days.

4. Referral attribution and prohibited methods

The program uses the Affiliate's assigned promotion code. A qualifying order must contain that code when the order is created. A Company referral link may place the code in a first-party browser cookie for up to 30 days. Cookies may be blocked, cleared or replaced, and the shopper may change or remove the code before checkout. A click alone does not create a commission. No lifetime customer ownership or entitlement to future orders is created. Only one affiliate receives attribution for an order.

An Affiliate's purchases and purchases using the Affiliate's own account or email do not qualify. The Affiliate must not conceal self-referrals through other accounts, reimburse buyers to manufacture commissions, submit fictitious orders, use stolen payment information, stuff cookies, force redirects, place unauthorized tracking, or interfere with another affiliate's attribution. Posting codes to coupon aggregators, bargain forums or unauthorized extensions requires prior written Company approval. Unsolicited bulk messaging, unlawful tracking, deceptive advertisements and unauthorized use of another person's data are prohibited.

The Company's saved order and acceptance records are the starting point for attribution. The Affiliate may request review of an apparent error within 60 days after the relevant statement becomes available and provide supporting evidence without sending payment credentials or unnecessary customer information. The Company will investigate in good faith and explain any correction. Neither a tracking error nor a suspected breach authorizes arbitrary forfeiture of otherwise valid commissions.

5. Commission calculation and eligibility

The commission rate is the rate in the Program Schedule accepted by the Affiliate and applicable when the qualifying order is created. Commission is calculated on the amount actually paid for eligible products after discounts, excluding sales tax, shipping charges, refunds, credits and canceled items. Calculations use U.S. dollars and round each order's commission to the nearest cent. Discount percentages offered to customers are separate from the Affiliate's commission percentage.

An order is eligible only if the Affiliate was approved, not suspended, and had accepted the then-current agreement version when it was created; the order was attributed as described above; and the Company has confirmed successful payment. Sandbox, internal test, fraudulent, unpaid and self-referred orders are excluded. The hold period in the Program Schedule begins with the first recorded payment confirmation. Commission does not become payable while a material payment dispute, suspected fraud or unresolved refund prevents verification of the qualifying amount.

Customer fraud, unauthorized-card use, friendly fraud, processor decisions and other chargebacks may occur without fault by either the Company or the Affiliate. The Company may temporarily hold only the commission reasonably associated with a disputed order while the dispute is unresolved. It will provide the affected order reference, reason and amount without disclosing unnecessary customer or payment information. A chargeback allegation alone is not a finding of Affiliate misconduct. The Company will review outstanding holds at least every 30 days and provide a status update on request. If the Company retains or recovers the qualifying payment, the corresponding commission will be released on the next scheduled payout after the ordinary hold period; the dispute does not restart that ordinary hold period. If a refund or final chargeback reduces the qualifying amount retained by the Company, the related commission may be reduced or reversed even where the cause was outside the Company's control. Processor fines, dispute fees and losses beyond the affected commission are not charged to an Affiliate solely because a customer disputes a transaction; any separate recovery for the Affiliate's own misconduct must be supported under this Agreement and applicable law.

Refunds, final chargebacks, cancellations and substantiated calculation errors may reduce or reverse the affected commission. Partial refunds require calculation against the remaining qualifying product amount. If an affected commission has already been paid, the Company will identify the reason and amount in a statement and may offset that amount against future commissions or request repayment. No adjustment may exceed the commission affected by the underlying event, and there will be no double recovery. Unrelated, undisputed commissions remain payable.

Portal figures are operational reports and may change with payment verification, refunds and corrections. An eligibility figure is not a receipt for a payout. The Company will maintain records of payments and adjustments and make an explanation available to the Affiliate on request.

6. Payments and tax information

Approved, undisputed commissions totaling at least $500 are payable every 30 days, through the methods specified in the accepted Program Schedule. The first payout date will be stated in the approval notice or account, with subsequent payment dates at 30-day intervals. The ordinary commission hold period is separate from this payment schedule; an amount that becomes payable after a cutoff carries to the next scheduled payout. Amounts below $500 carry forward and are not forfeited solely because the threshold has not been reached, subject to the final-payment provisions on termination. Before any payout, the Affiliate must have accepted this Agreement and supplied complete, accurate payee instructions and the applicable tax documentation through the Company-designated secure channel. U.S. payees must provide a properly completed and signed Form W-9; non-U.S. payees must provide the applicable tax certification requested by the Company. The Company issues any required information returns, including Form 1099 where applicable; signing a Form 1099 is not an enrollment or payout requirement. Payment timing depends on completion of these requirements. The Company will identify missing information and will not request full tax identifiers, bank credentials or identity documents through an ordinary support message or public source repository. Sensitive documents must be supplied through the secure method designated by the Company.

Each party is responsible for its own reporting and tax obligations. The Company may withhold amounts when required by law and will provide applicable reporting. Changes to payee instructions may require separate verification. The Affiliate must promptly report suspected payment-instruction fraud. Payments are not considered made merely because a portal shows eligible commissions; actual payment records control. Processor delays or rejected transfers will be investigated and retried after valid instructions are confirmed.

7. Confidentiality and information security

Nonpublic business information, unreleased materials, security information and information expressly identified as confidential must be used only for participation in the program and protected with reasonable care. This obligation does not cover information lawfully public, independently developed, previously known without restriction or lawfully received from another source. Legally required disclosures are permitted, with prior notice where lawful.

The Affiliate must safeguard account access, avoid sharing credentials and promptly notify the Company of suspected compromise. Affiliate reports do not grant access to shoppers' personal information. The Affiliate may not collect or request customer payment information on the Company's behalf. Each party must comply with applicable privacy and marketing laws for information it independently handles. On termination, the Affiliate must cease use of Company confidential information and delete or return it, except records required by law or reasonably retained to document payment rights.

8. Suspension and termination

Either party may terminate participation by written notice, including an authenticated account communication. The Company may suspend new referrals while investigating a reasonable concern involving fraud, unlawful content, security or a material breach. It will identify the concern where doing so would not compromise an investigation or violate law. For a remediable breach, the Company will ordinarily allow a reasonable opportunity to correct it. Immediate suspension or termination is permitted where continued activity creates material legal, security or fraud risk.

Upon termination, the Affiliate must stop presenting itself as an active affiliate and stop using Company marks, materials, links and codes. Termination does not cancel valid commissions earned on qualifying orders created before termination. Those commissions remain subject to the accepted hold period, refunds and verification. The Company will settle the final undisputed balance, including a balance below the normal payout minimum, within 60 days after the applicable hold period ends and required payment information is complete. Disputed amounts will be resolved separately without delaying undisputed amounts.

9. Responsibility and claims

Each party is responsible for its own unlawful conduct, negligence, unauthorized representations and breach of this Agreement. To the extent permitted by law, a party will indemnify the other against third-party claims and reasonable defense costs to the extent caused by its fraud, willful misconduct, violation of law, or infringement through materials it supplied without authorization. The protected party must give prompt notice, allow reasonable participation in the defense and cooperate at the defending party's expense. No settlement may admit fault by, impose nonmonetary duties on, or require payment from the protected party without its consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

To the extent permitted by law, neither party is liable for speculative lost profits or indirect or consequential losses arising from participation. This exclusion does not limit payment of earned commissions, fraud, willful misconduct, infringement, misuse of confidential information, obligations concerning third-party claims under this section, or liability that applicable law does not permit the parties to exclude. Nothing in this Agreement represents that unlawful claims become permissible through a disclaimer or indemnity.

10. Changes and records

The Company may publish revised program terms under a new version. Material changes to compensation, payment timing or participation obligations require notice and affirmative acceptance before applying to new orders for that Affiliate. The Company may pause new referral eligibility until acceptance. Changes do not retroactively reduce an earned commission or replace the version governing an earlier order. Immediate restrictions on unlawful or unsafe promotional conduct may take effect upon notice, without changing previously earned compensation.

The Company retains the accepted text, Program Schedule, version and acceptance time. Affiliates may retain or print a copy and request their acceptance record. Continuing to use an account does not by itself constitute acceptance of a materially revised financial schedule. A separately signed agreement expressly identifying the conflicting provision controls that provision; an informal conversation or portal estimate does not silently amend this Agreement.

11. Notices and general terms

Program notices may be delivered through the authenticated account and the Affiliate's registered email. The Company's program contact is the address displayed in the Program Schedule. Each party must maintain a functioning notice address and report changes. The parties will first attempt in good faith to resolve a dispute through written notice and discussion for 30 days, without preventing urgent relief or a timely filing needed to preserve a claim.

Applicable law and any court's jurisdiction are determined under the otherwise applicable conflict-of-laws and jurisdiction rules; this Agreement does not impose mandatory arbitration or a class-action waiver. A provision found unenforceable will be enforced to the lawful extent, and the remaining provisions remain effective. Failure to enforce a provision once does not waive later enforcement. Neither party may assign participation to another person without the other's written consent, except a Company transfer of the program with its business that preserves accrued payment obligations and gives notice. This Agreement and the accepted Program Schedule are the complete agreement concerning participation, subject to any expressly controlling signed agreement. Accrued payment rights, confidentiality, claims, recordkeeping and provisions intended by their nature to survive will survive termination.
